top_stories.title: Hajj pilgrims gather at Mount Arafat under scorching desert sun | Religion News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Thousands** of Muslims gathered at Mount Arafat for the most important ritual of the Hajj pilgrimage, facing scorching desert temperatures near 40 degrees Celsius.  The annual event, which draws over 1.5 million pilgrims this year, is obligatory for all physically and financially able Muslims. Despite a war between the United States and Israel against Iran casting a shadow across the Middle East, Saudi officials reported more pilgrims from abroad than in 2024. Volunteers provided water, food, and shade to the pilgrims making their way to Mount Arafat.

top_stories.title: 'Unjust and unfounded': Mango founder's son denies killing father, steps down as vice president - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Jonathan Andic**, son of late Mango founder **Isak Andic**, has stepped down as vice president of the fashion giant's board to focus on his legal defense after being arrested in Spain as part of an investigation into his father's death.  **Andic** denies any involvement in his father's death, calling the accusations "serious, unjust and unfounded." The case was reopened in October 2025 after investigators found inconsistencies in **Andic**'s statements and the circumstances surrounding the fall. Authorities are also investigating potential tensions between the father and son related to Isak Andic's plans for a charitable foundation.

top_stories.title: US senator says he was pepper-sprayed by federal agents during protest at ICE facility | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Senator Andy Kim** and **Governor Mikie Sherrill**, both Democrats, joined protests outside an immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, where they witnessed clashes with federal agents.  Kim reported being pepper-sprayed by ICE officials while attempting to de-escalate a situation involving protesters and agents. Demonstrators allege detainees have been denied food, medical care, and air conditioning at the facility, prompting a hunger strike and work stoppage. **Department of Homeland Security (DHS)** Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** denied claims of a hunger strike, stating that conditions are not sub-prime.  The protests come amid stalled efforts to pass a funding measure for ICE and border patrol, with Senate Republicans blocking the bill due to disagreements over Trump's plans for a White House ballroom and a "anti-weaponization" fund.

top_stories.title: Diplomacy, new war technology vital to deter India, say experts - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Academicians, diplomats, military and war experts** gathered at the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad (ISSI) to discuss the importance of diplomacy in maintaining strategic stability in South Asia. **Professor Dr Zafar Nawaz Jaspal**, **Vice Chancellor of Quaid-e-Azam University,** emphasized the need for sustained dialogue between India and Pakistan for regional peace, noting that the current deadlock has hindered confidence-building measures and arms control.  **Dr Rizwana Abbasi**, a professor at NUML's Department of International Relations, highlighted how India's evolving military posture and new technologies are increasing regional instability. **Air Commodore (Retd.) Khalid Banuri** discussed the changing character of war with the emergence of AI, hypersonic missiles, and space-based systems, emphasizing the need for human oversight in decision-making processes.  **Maj. top_stories.title: Israel is no longer ‘shooting and crying’ | Crimes Against Humanity | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: The recent revelations about the brutal torture of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails, including rape and sexual violence, have exposed a disturbing reality of Palestinian life under Israeli occupation.  **Israeli** guards are documented committing these acts while laughing, raising concerns about the normalization of such behavior within society. This gleeful violence is not unique to this instance but has been a trend since the 2010s, with **Israelis** celebrating their soldiers' efficiency in killing Palestinians and viewing such actions as rewarding.  The article argues that this glee stems from a deeply ingrained settler colonial worldview that dehumanizes Palestinians and associates violence with rewards, ultimately leading to a society that celebrates and embraces such atrocities.

top_stories.title: Quote of the day by Nelson Mandela: “If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head. If you talk to him in his language, that goes to his heart.” | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Nelson Mandela's** quote, "If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head. If you talk to him in his language, that goes to his heart," explores the distinction between understanding information and feeling connected emotionally through shared language or cultural experiences. The quote highlights how communication transcends mere linguistic exchange and emphasizes the importance of recognizing another person's unique perspective and background. This resonates with people because it speaks to a fundamental human need for connection and recognition.

top_stories.title: Woman shot dead outside Sheffield bar was innocent bystander, police say | UK news | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: **South Yorkshire police** are investigating the fatal shooting of a 30-year-old woman outside a Sheffield bar. The victim, an innocent bystander celebrating the bank holiday weekend, was found with serious injuries and later died in hospital. **Ch Supt Jamie Henderson**, district commander for Sheffield, stated that two men and a woman have been arrested on suspicion of murder, while police are appealing for witnesses who were in the area around 2:45 am Monday morning.

top_stories.title: North Korea fired projectiles, including short-range ballistic missile, Seoul says - World - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **North Korea** fired several projectiles, including at least one short-range ballistic missile, toward waters off its west coast on Tuesday. The **South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff** said the missiles flew about 80 kilometers and are North Korea's first known launch since April 19th.  **South Korea’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson** urged North Korea to respond to peace overtures and reduce tensions, while Seoul maintained its goal of complete denuclearization.

top_stories.title: Albert Manifold ousted as BP chair over governance and conduct concerns | Oil and Gas News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **BP** chairman Albert Manifold has been ousted after only eight months on the job due to "serious concerns" regarding governance standards, oversight, and conduct. The **board** made the decision unanimously, with interim chair Ian Tyler taking over immediately.  This follows a series of leadership changes at the oil and gas giant, including the abrupt departure of CEO Murray Auchincloss and former CEO Bernard Looney. BP's stock is down in both US and UK markets following the announcement.

top_stories.title: ‘Just take it away’: Mother of teen who died after alleged TikTok challenge urges UK govt to ban social media - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ellen Roome**, whose 14-year-old son Jools Sweeney died in 2022 after attempting a dangerous online challenge, is urging the **UK government** to take immediate action on restricting children's access to social media.  She and other bereaved parents will meet with **Prime Minister Keir Starmer** on Tuesday as a national consultation on a possible social media ban for under-16s nears its conclusion.  **Wes Streeting**, former UK health secretary, has also called for stricter regulation of social media platforms, comparing them to the tobacco industry and highlighting the potential harm caused by excessive use among children. **TikTok** is facing legal action in the US from families who lost children due to a dangerous online challenge, with Roome calling for access to platform data to understand what content their children were exposed to.
